Replacing none with a skip adds a free residual path, whereas replacing a conv with a skip typically loses accuracy.
Removing a conv from the direct edge costs far more than removing a skip or pool.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 has no route to the output, so a conv on edge 1 is wasted.
With edge 5 removed, edge 2's output never reaches node 3, so the conv is wasted.
Edge 4 reads node 1, which is empty when edge 0 is none, so the conv is useless.
With edge 0 removed, edge 2 reads an input that is only partly fed, so the conv adds little.
Adding conv3x3 where there was no edge increases connectivity to the output more than replacing a skip or pool.
Activating edge 4 from none adds a new conv path through node 1 to the output, gaining more than swapping ops.
Activating edge 1 from none adds a new path into node 2, gaining more than swapping one op for another.
